reviews.review_msg: Super chill prof, exams are straight forward. Just do the practice questions he assigns along with reviewing the in class exercises and you'll be good. Lectures are okay, however he does make them entertaining by making jokes.

Nice person, but very unorganized. We had a presentation worth 35% and all we had to go off was previous years examples, no rubric. Further instructions were added 24 hours before presenting. He was also on his phone during every presentation and told us that in previous years the highest mark went to the nicest looking PowerPoint and not content.

Literally better off not going to lecture. He constantly goes off on rants that are vaguely related to the course and doesn't teach you anything that is going to be on the tests. He gives practice exams at least.

Ray is a good prof. He focuses on teaching the core concepts of the course instead of giving long lectures on theory. Provides with homework and practice questions which are similar to exam questions. Textbook not required. Overall a solid choice.

I took BUS 322 in Fall and found Ray is a fair professor. He does not walk you through step-by-step for practice questions cause you can learn ALL calculations in his TA's notes which is given. Be careful, he drops hints in lecture which essay questions will be on exams. Final is harder than midterm. Group is self-construced, wisely choose members.

DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS. WORST PROF I'VE EVER SEEN. Unorganized at all. You dont need him to learn the course, and you pay the tuition for self-studying. No one else would be worse than him. If you see his name when enrolling coursestake the course next time, please. I dont comment on his grading, but he is definitely a bad lecturer.

Easily the most unorganized professor I have had in my time at SFU. His lectures are also all qualitative and then the exams are completely quantitative so you have to study on your own a lot. However, the exams are easy if you read the textbook and do the homework questions. During presentations, he was either on his phone or about to fall asleep.
Terrible. Does not know what he is talking about. No interest in the subject. Uses handphone all the time
He's a very nice professor, who provides detailed descriptions of knowledge and practical feedback.
Ray is a nice guy. He is glad to help students. Although he is relatively new in Beedie for teaching, accounting seems to be his profession.

This professor had no idea what he was talking about and was incredibly disorganized. Incorrect solutions were posted for homework questions and he did not write his own exams. Marking was very unfair; part marks were not given for any questions. The professor was on his phone during our presentations and refused to answer questions during exams.

Group presentation component required coordination that was challenging. Instructor offered extra office hours before the final which were very helpful for understanding course material. Exam was comprehensive but appropriate for an advanced accounting course. Would recommend attending office hours.

I appreciated the attempts for interactive activities, but, they didn't work in a class of 70. Excel walkthroughs were helpful but challenging in the small room. Glad there were lots of solutions to practice questions (all excel files in class had solution tabs and there were PDFs in every unit with solutions to all the even-numbered questions)

Lisa provides practice problems with no solutions. To check our work, she recommends forming study groups and comparing answers with our peers. She does not spend much time teaching, instead students watch sustainability themed group projects and do random activities. Exam questions were were unexpected: 3 hours + take home portion.

One of few Profs at Beedie I know actually has experience with CPA program. Some challenging critical thinking questions during class and as part of the exams but most of the main exam questions were nearly identical to the spreadsheet questions we were given in class. Do the Excel questions you are given in class and you'll be fine.

I see a lot of people switching their reviews after grades were released. As someone who got an A+ in the course (solely due to the curve), I still think reviews should be based on the teaching capacity of the professor, not your individual grade. Lisa was a disorganized and rude professor, she overworked us and provided no help or resources.

Nice prof, kind but not very organized and heavy on sustainability.

No homework, 1 group paper (pick members wisely), and 2 textbooks. 

Concepts are easy but lots of self-learning. 

Tests are dense and tightly timed. 

Be direct when asking questions and ask follow-ups—she tends to go on tangents.
Final grade came out, and I did better than expected. Forgive me, Lisa. Perhaps I was too harsh.

I know there is a lot of negative comments about Lisa, but most of them came ahead of the final grades. I came out of the class with a newfound appreciation for sustainability reporting accounting. The problem is that this class is an intermediate managerial accounting course first, and I had trouble finding the synergies between the two concepts.

After seeing my grade I take back my previous 1 star. Lisa is coolios, just not the typical structure of an accounting course you'd expect. However, the difficulty of the content isn't heavy compared to other accounting courses. Usually I get Cs in accounting, but dropped an A- today... so seems like course is doable in the end! Practice & engage!

Lisa wasn't a bad prof, but the course was just not for me. She advised everyone to get Pearson (~$110) which I did, but wasn't that useful for the exams (both midterm and final). Better to study first using the handouts she gives and use free trial of Pearson. She mainly breezes through the slides and class activities rather managerial problems

It is clear that she is very passionate about what she teaches. However I think she needs to spend more time engaging students with accounting lessons rather than sustainability lessons. Exam would have been fair if we had 4-5 hours instead of 3, way too long of an exam for 3 hours.

I had 320 with Dennis and he was inspirational to pursue my degree in accounting. 

Lisa was not inspirational and is the reason I want to drop out of accounting.
She is an excellent instructor. If you have questions, attend office hours; she explains everything clearly. To those with concerns, I'd suggest trying her office hours first.

One of the worst accounting profs I've had. Lectures focus on sustainability talk instead of actual course material. Practice questions are dumped at the end with no guidance, and the final tested the hardest concepts we were barely taught. Avoid at all costs.

Doesn't explain anything clearly, not even during office hours. Almost as if she doesn't know what she is talking about, she dodges questions and says to look at the textbook or class notes. Class notes don't exist and she doesn't provide solutions to practice problems. Exam was 3 hours + take home portion. No respect for students time or effort.

Over emphasis on sustainability. You spend most of your time on group projects that are mainly about sustainability and spend less than a third of the class on managerial accounting concepts - all while the exams are 90% on managerial accounting that she barely goes over.

If you want to actually learn managerial accounting I'd skip her.

Incredibly frustrating professor that made the course a far worse time than big 4 busy season. Incredibly difficult exam that was impossible to finish in 3 hours. Always answered students with “see textbook” or something ridiculous. If you value your time, sanity, effort, avoid this professor AT ALL COSTS. Also, did not provide answers to questions

This professor was an absolute nightmare, it was so bad, that I felt the need to make this review. Incredibly long and impossible final exam that was no where NEAR fair. Answered students with “see textbook” and provided no solutions to practice questions. DO NOT TAKE, if you value your sanity and grades. Was a better time in PwC during busy season

This is the first time I haven't finished an exam. Final was impossible to do in 3hrs and even included a take-home section. Haven't taken 312 and was put at a major disadvantage when she jumped into capital budgeting Qs w/o explaining (most important topic btw). Too many projects, 30-40 min seminars were stupid and ate up valuable class time 0/10

Final exam was insane. 4 just brutally lengthy questions, including one where the question itself was 4 pages long, and the required calculations/answers were split up into ~20 parts. Majority of people didn't even finish. She yelled at a student for asking to use the bathroom. Would be surprised if the average was above 40%.

She obviously cares a lot about accounting, but she teaches the class terribly. Tries to make everything into a game that provides no learning value. Provides us with complex practice problems but no answers and refuses to explain them. The final exam felt like a prank, the only people who left early were ones who gave up and didnt finish.

Sure, Lisa was disorganized, took forever to grade, was inconsistent with marking, and wouldn't post solutions. But she's a first-year prof, and most of you wouldn't understand how tough that is—especially teaching a class with a campus celeb. Tom Brady was a 6th-round pick and struggled early. I think Lisa could be the next GOAT of SFU profs.

Very organized with clear instructions for all assignments. The workload is fair and matches course goals. Though the content is challenging, she supports learning by posting class solutions. Expectations are clear, and grading is consistent with no surprises. She makes the course structured and easy to follow.
Really good she teaches us how to study and the importance of working with your peers

Hardest final exam I have ever done. Doesn't help that she didn't explain any topics, or provide any answers to practice problems. Exam was way too long for a 3hour exam, so many people didn't finish, and she provided little to no support leading up to it. Told us to ask her questions and her responses wer "check your notes" or check the textbook

Nice lady, but terrible prof. Instead of teaching the class normally, she decides to turn everything into an interactive adventure game, which results in no learning. Tons of assignments, very extensive projects, and exams are brutal to study for. Spends 99% of the time talking about sustainability even though it makes up 5-10% of the exam.

Unorganized, and does not grade our work on time. Has made the exams harder than she said they would be, and was not helpful in terms of exam prep. The course concepts are not that hard with the work, but the exams do not reflect what's learned.

Absolutely worst prof in Beedie. We've covered 0 topic in class, solved 0 problems, only talked about sustainability. No solutions to practice questions. Literally nobody in class is following the course. Avoid at all costs

I never thought I'd be posting on one of these, but what this prof needs is to create a sustainability podcast or something to an audience of 50-100 viewers rather than her 50-100 accounting students. 5 years in this program and by far this was the most horrific experience yet. Brutal.
Not a good idea....

The worst Prof I've come across ever. She teaches nothing related to the course or the exams in class. Does not give out solutions to practice questions as she wants you to figure out the correct answers by working with your peers, but would you ever know if the answer is correct... Talked more about sustainability than accounting.
DO NOT TAKE HER!!!

Nice person, genuinely an awful professor though. Heavy workload, teaches ESG more than accounting, completely disorganized, and not helpful at all. Will spend 5-10 mins giving you an answer to a completely unrelated question from the one you asked, that will leave you more confused. Very unclear about expectations for assignments/papers/tests etc

Dude this prof hasn't taught me anything. For our last chapter (she said super important for the final) all she provided was an excel question and doesn't explain how to get the answers and the logic behind it ( she said any practice we do for this question will be nothing compared to the exam difficulty). Better off learning from Khan academy

She is very passionate about accounting, but her teaching has to be the worst teaching I've ever encountered. Classes are pretty much useless and off-topic, weekly assignments that will have you consumed and overwhelmed, and hard to understand practice problems that only leaves you more confused. Lisa should try a traditional teaching style.

Lisa is very disorganized. Besides, the course load is unreasonably heavy: seminar, discussions, term paper, homework, tests, and participation. Does not teach Managerial accounting, therefore it is confusing what to expect from the final. Need major improvement.
talks for hours about nothing

Extremely disorganized - vague instructions for assignments. Heavy workload for no reason. Content is easy but she makes it hard to practice (doesn't post in-class solutions out of fear of someone leaking them). Seems like she doesn't even know what she wants students to do. Every deliverable grading incident is a unpredictable surprise

So disorganized. She cares and is nice but there is way too much going on. Would not recommend. Rather than teach and assign practice problems, she gives time to do problems in class (does not really provide solutions) and expects students to learn on their own.

Lisa is a subpar accounting professor; she would be my fifth accounting professor I have had, and by far the one with the least pleasant experience with her. First, her lectures are slow and unorganized; she gets very frustrated very easily when lectures aren't going her way (probably cause unorganized). Tests are fair but that's it.

Not a great experience as one who prefers not to self-teach the material for an in-person course. Difficult to follow along 200-slide ppts, with 90% being Excel screenshots (not explained well, either). Exams don't fully match assigned practice. 1 hour group-led seminars on sustainability take up time that could be for doing practice questions.

Claims that the slides are "for my teaching and not your learning". She doesn't teach concepts she just points at excel screenshots with minimal explanations. 1 hour seminar on sustainability at the end of every class (mandatory attendance). Midterm and final are extremely difficult and content doesn't match practice/assigned questions.

The course content isn't difficult on its own, but the professor makes it much harder than it needs to be. Her explanations are unclear and she doesn't add value in lectures. Exams cover material or question types we never saw in class or homework. If you're someone who needs clear instruction and fair exams, avoid this professor.

Don't take this class with her, just wait for a good prof. The midterm was alright but the final was like 30 pages long and so confusing not because the concepts are difficult, rather it was due to her not being able to word questions properly.

In my personal opinion, one of the least organized professors I have had for accounting. Lectures are extremely hard to follow and she provides excel solutions to practise questions which make it very hard to understand (much harder then it should be.)

I have taken a couple of accounting classes with her. She provides a lot of resources that requires tons of reading and prep but she is very caring and helpful both inside and outside the classroom. Getting a good grade is definitely possible if you spend the time and effort she expects.
She has really long slides with excel screenshot of examples. The lectures are not really helpful, you will need a lot of self study. Fair exams but pretty long.

She's very nice but her exams were somewhat difficult and in class just reads off slides (which are nothing like the exams). There's a huge group project and another one as well but its related to sustainability and balanced scorecard concepts when really, I'd prefer to just do accounting practice! I felt like I only learned fluff in this class.

FYI think she read the reviews and made changes to her exams. Midterm was okay, but final exam was hilariously difficult. The questions she provides has nothing to do with the exams lol. 

Term paper and presentation had high averages and weren't too troublesome though. 

She replies to emails pretty quick so there's that.

Pray for the curve boys

Terrible instructor that has no teaching skills. This is a self taught course and it is pointless to show up to lecture. You gain no benefit from attending lecture. Her lectures actually make you even more confused.
Fereshteh is a great prof. She is very caring, approachable, and easy to talk to.

Fereshteh is really nice but can be disorganized at times. Exams have really high averages, around 80-85% and the term paper and presentation averages were even higher, around 90%. You literally have to get perfect scores on everything for an A. Although she's approachable, when I asked her questions at office hours, I left even more confused lol

I had Bus 320 and 322 with her. I like her as a person but as a prof i think she still has areas to work on. Her finals averages are SUPER high, like 80-84, with basically you have to do well to get just an average. The term paper for both classes had super high averages too.
One of the nicest accounting profs. I took BUS 320 and BUS 322 with her. She provides a lot of notes and her powerpoints are very helpful and clear. She is always available for help if you need it.

Ray is the goat no other way to put. If you're not good at accounting then it will still be a difficult class. But his lecturers are amazing and if you pay attention you will learn things that you would otherwise only learn working after graduation.
Good Professor.
funny and gives good examples that back up the material. is giving us a pizza party on the last day. shoutout ray zhang

A bit disorganized, but he is very effective at synthesizing the textbook information and providing lots of relevant examples during lectures. if you take him, go to class! he's a pretty chill dude too.

Ray is a nice person, but his class is very unorganized. There is a presentation worth quite a significant chunk of your grade, yet no criteria or rubric was provided for it. The guidelines (e.g., how long it should be) for the presentation were sent out with less than 24 hours' notice before the presentation date.

Safia is a super nice prof! The content is not super difficult compared to the other 300-level acc courses. The midterm is quite easy, but final was a bit more difficult. Make sure to do the questions and practice exams she provides and you will be set! Find a good group for the presentation, and ask clarifying questions. Curve is relatively high.

She is awful and should not be teaching at a Post secondary level
She is difficult to understand due to her strong accent. When asked a question, she never knows the answers.
Avoid her if possible. You are better off reading your text book that attending her classes as she just reads her slides that gets forn the text book.  You will be on your own

the worst prof  i have ever had in sfu. she reads the slides, without adding any extra explanation. regret for the whole semester because i need to study all the materials by myself. and she is never available in her office hour.
She read slides, nothing else. Her accent is really heavy, and she could not answer questions properly because her English is terrible.

He teaches everything from the book. he doesn't make his own slides and uses the slides that comes with the book. Class is not hard, but boring.U will not learn anything in his class. Avoid at any cost.

Let's face it, managerial accounting is a fairly dry course, but Francisco did a great job in making the class interesting through case studies and presentations as well as examples from his career past. The exams were fair and I felt well prepared. This is a professor that wants you to succeed and I'm glad I took the course with him!
REALLY NICE GUY, ALTHOUGH HAVE ACCENT, BUT HE IS REALLY NICE!FOCUS ON HIS NOTES, AND MAKE SURE YOU DO ALL THE HOMEWORK, THEN YOU WILL BE GOOD IN THIS CLASS! PRETTY FAIR EXAMS~

Very disappointed with this professor. Does not have a helpful attitude towards students and is extremely unclear with his expectations. He loves the subject (managerial accounting), but he makes the exams unreasonably difficult. If you wish to take this course will him, then good luck - you'll need it.

His classes are very boring. It is hard to understand him sometimes. During lectures and tutorial he just goes over notes, which are all posted, making attendance sort of useless. Multiple choice questions are on the tricky side.

He's a good person who cares about students. However, his exams are too difficult. they are very discouraging. even if you practice all the tutorial questions you can still do poorly on the exam... not recommended for 322.

He is a very fair professor. He is helpful when you ask him questions that are concise and clear, and easy to get a long. This class is hard due to content, but Kamlani tries his best to help us understand all the material. It was helpful having him as my TA. His tests are difficult, but you really need to push yourself to understand the material.

He must have realized the midterm was so difficult that he made the final very very much easier. The # of theory questions on the final made me feel like I was sitting thru an OB exam rather than an accounting one. 20min into the lectures, and you'll find yourself still staring at the 1st ppt slide.

I thought the midterm was insanely hard and poorly worded, but the final was much more fair. Lectures were dull/unclear and I stopped attending, my friends detailed notes from Professor Spector was a must.

Prof gets nervous, hes nice and tries to help you out as much as he can but material is very dry and lectures are boring (as are most managerial classes). Midterm is more quantitative and final qualitative. textbook is useful if you dont pay attention.
pretty decent prof, a little boring at times but very clear and thorough... maybe too thorough

Okay, guys. If you take this class with him, be prepared. He fills his lectures with "useless" details about garbage... doesn't even have a CMA; even if you have an MBA you shouldn't be teaching an upper level manag. acct course. Also -- DOESN'T USE SLIDESHOW FEATURE ON POWERPOINT. That tells you all you need to know right there.
Fun teacher
not that easy.. essay questions on exams..feel like a HR course..he's a nice guy though..

he's nice. Always try to help students, and answers quickly especially on his email. course was annoying since it's a new course, but he's nice. anyway if you are doing accoutning major, you gotta face this course. take it with him.

Inspirational. Future teachers should take notice as to what not to do when teaching. Rubic unclear so i spent a chunk of time lost and confused. Was again reflected when students were incorrectly assigned in Canva. Does half a practice problem of a hard question and decides to put that type of question it on the exam. say wallahi bro - ishowspeed.

I think I would eat rotten fruits and vegetables than be in this class. I have gained a new appreciation for my life after spending time in this lecture. However, she is a hilarious professor not because of her jokes but rather the way she talks and expects us not to fall asleep. One of the most passive aggressive profs ever. -Pyara G
DON'T Take her class pls!!!!!!
DON'T Take her class pls!!!!!!

Incredibly kind professor! Although he reads from his slides during lectures, but his exams are fair — cheat sheets are allowed! For written questions (20%), copy down all sample problems from his slides; he only changes the numbers. But MC questions (80%) are brutally detailed and require thorough knowledge of the material. SO READ YOUR TEXTBOOK!
Weiming liu is very very good he explains things very well

He's a nice guy but he spoke to his TA in Chinese… His English isn't great so it can be hard to understand what he's talking about and he doesn't seem to have any pedagogical skills. The course also included too much content, you aren't able to actually learn intuitively and understand, hence the cheat sheet.

Such a genuinely nice guy who tries his best to make managerial accounting fun. The class is a lot of work but his tests are very fair and easier than the content covered in lecture. Definitely recommend!
Pretty good professor to study accounting with at Beedie!
He is the best.
